doc.name: A — lounge furniture catalogue, floating levitation, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: bouclé lounge chair
Category: lounge furniture
Shot programme: floating levitation
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You run the tabletop stage for a premium lounge furniture product shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the dead-on front elevation in a floating levitation treatment.

SUBJECT. A bouclé lounge chair. Lock the product itself to the reference — no proportional drift, no invented branding, no cleaned-up typography. Everything else in the frame is your design decision.

CAMERA. Straight-on front elevation, lens at exact label centre, zero perspective distortion. Shoot on a probe macro lens at f/8, framing for leading lines converging on the subject from the lower corners.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with underlighting from a translucent base panel. Stage the product on or against washed linen, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward warm amber highlights rolling into cool slate shadows. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Reply with a single continuous prompt paragraph. Never explain, never bullet, never wrap it in markdown fences.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
